newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA sees minor jobs impact from labour reform.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA sees minor jobs impact from labour reform.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Ian Macfarlane said on Wednesday that it was quite possible that passage of the government's industrial relations bill in parliament would have very little effect on employment, with most of the effect seen on productivity.
"Can I say I am agnostic on that," Macfarlane told an economists' conference in Canberra when asked about the implications of the legislation on employment.
"It is quite possible that it will have very little effect on employment and most of the effect will be on productivity and long-run growth," he said.
The Workplace Relations Bill is set to face heated debate in parliament's upper house, the Senate, later this year where the government does not have a clear majority.

The opposition Labor Party, which lost the March 1996 election and campaigned against the bill, has said it would oppose the legislation while the government has begun talks with the minority Australian Democrats party to win their support.
The bill reduces the impact of the union movement and introduces employer-worker negotiations as a centrepiece of the industrial relations system.
